Subject: Benchmarking & close plan: performance playbook for hosted / dedicated / private

Tim — following up on last week's call. Attached is our proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and a short performance benchmarking playbook focused on the metrics you asked about: latency (P50/P95/P99), time-to-first-token (TTFT), sustained throughput, and concurrency/isolation under mixed workloads. High-level items and asks: 

- Scope: run identical evals across Hosted (managed API tier), Dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and Private (customer VPC) using your sample prompt set and two traffic profiles (interactive chat & batch inference).
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, max sustainable TPS, cold-start behavior, KV-cache hit rates, and autoscale reaction (time to scale and queue growth).
- Isolation tests: run noisy-neighbor stress (co-located synthetic load) against Hosted to show predictability delta vs Dedicated/Private.
- Timeline: 2-week eval window (env prep + run + analysis). Proposed dates in MAP_v1.xlsx.
- Responsibilities: Acme to provide test tenant + sample dataset, Redwood to run the harness and provide dashboards + raw logs.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP + timelines), sample harness config.

Next steps: if the plan looks good we schedule the tenant handoff (Lauren will coordinate access) and target an exec readout the week after runs complete.

Thanks —
Markus Klein

Team / Tim — sharing a short summary from the initial runs we completed against Acme's sample prompts (runs executed in Redwood's staging harness). Raw CSV attached and Grafana dashboards linked. High-level findings: 

Summary (median of 3 passes, interactive profile):
- Hosted (managed API): P50=48ms, P95=220ms, P99=420ms, TTFT=140ms, sustained throughput ~250 TPS (token-limited), autoscale reaction ~90s (queue observable at 70% load). Isolation: noisy-neighbor injection increased P95 by ~45% during peak bursts.
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs): P50=20ms, P95=75ms, P99=110ms, TTFT=45ms, sustained throughput ~900 TPS, autoscale N/A (fixed pool). Isolation: stable under injected noise; latencies increased <5%.
- Private (customer VPC): P50=22ms, P95=80ms, P99=120ms, TTFT=55ms, sustained throughput ~850 TPS (network variance observed), autoscale behavior depends on your cluster config — in our tests with your suggested autoscaler it scaled in ~60–120s depending on warm cache.

Interpretation: Dedicated gives clear latency and throughput predictability; Private is close but has more network variance depending on VPC peering and KMS latency; Hosted is fine for lighter interactive workloads but shows variability under noisy neighbors and autoscale lag that can affect SLOs for bursty traffic.

Next steps / asks:
- Confirm which SLOs Acme wants prioritized (latency SLO vs cost per token).
- If you want a tighter Hosted SLO we can propose a Dedicated reserve + fallback policy in the MAP (can cut P95 by ~2–3x for critical routes).

Attachments: acme_hosted-vs-dedicated-raw.csv, acme_perf_summary_qc.pdf
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ACME/perf-dashboard
